references.text: Thematic parallel: The Lord's intervention gives a child to a woman who has been in distress or on the margins, ensuring a new generation.
Contrastive parallel: God's power to give life and blessing appears both in a holy line (Ruth) and through grace after sin (Bathsheba).
Moral contrast: Marriage and birth resulting from righteousness (Ruth) versus sin and judgment (Bathsheba).
Direct reference: Matt 1:5 confirms Ruth as an ancestor of Jesus, based on the event in Ruth 4:13.
Thematic parallel: God's use of women outside the traditional framework (Moabite/Hittite woman) to shape God's story, even with different emphases (blessing versus judgment).
Same event: Genealogical confirmation that Boaz became the father of Obed through Ruth.
Thematic parallel: The Lord's intervention to give a child to a woman who has waited and carried sorrow (Hannah and Ruth).
